customer_question: Our product is still in prototype, so we don't have a mass-production product name yet -- can registration proceed using just our internal development model name?
question_variants: Do we need to wait for our final product name before registering?
Can we use a working/internal name for the registration instead of the eventual retail name?
Is it possible to register a prototype before the product name is finalized?
actual_issue: A prototype-stage customer with no finalized mass-production product name yet needed to know whether Bluetooth SIG registration could proceed using the product's development-stage model name instead.
plain_english_explanation: Some products go through certification before their final retail name is even decided. Rather than waiting for that name, a registration can be filed using whatever internal name the product is currently known by during development, since SIG registration isn't restricted to using only the name a product will eventually be sold under.
consultant_answer: Yes, registration is not necessarily limited to only the model name a product will be sold under -- registering using a development-stage model name is acceptable.
decision_logic: Bluetooth SIG registration does not require a finalized, market-release product name; a development-stage or internal model name can be used for registration when the final name is not yet available.
final_recommendation: When a customer's product is still in development with no finalized product name, advise them that registration can proceed using their current development-stage model name.
risk_if_done_wrong: Telling a prototype-stage customer that registration must wait for a finalized product name would cause unnecessary delay to their certification timeline.
